description: Fleet-shared Renovate baseline (agent-lcars#1340 C2), consumed as
sprinkles, and sync-padd. Carries only the common core; genuinely
repo-local policy stays in each consumer's renovate.json.
nx-cache-server keeps its deliberately stricter pin-digests config and
www/girosf have no Renovate — both stay off this preset on purpose.
toolSettings.nodeMaxMemory (integer MiB, npm manager only) caps the Node
child processes Renovate spawns (pnpm lockfile/artifact updates), not
Renovate's own process. sprinkles' hosted job on 2026-09-15 used 3.0 GB
of Mend Community Cloud's 3.0 GB whole-job memory cap (11m of a 30m
execution limit); jobs that hit that cap are demoted to Mend's weekly
Blocked schedule until one clean run, consistent with sprinkles going
silent 2026-08-24 to 2026-09-15. The cap covers Renovate plus pnpm, so
this uses 1536, the bottom of Mend's recommended 1.5-2.5 GB range

packageRules.description: Group and automerge updates that preserve the declared compatibility range

Major updates are never merged unattended, whichever bot authors the PR: they open as DRAFT pull requests with auto-merge off. Every member repo's agent-automerge-reusable.yml treats a bot login as auto-mergeable the moment a non-draft PR is opened, and it deliberately leaves drafts alone (draft is the fleet's parked state), so draftPR is the guard. Kept when self-hosted Renovate was reverted (2026-09-21): it protects the hosted-app repos too -- without it the 2026-09-20 mariadb 12->13 bump would have auto-merged on green without the MARIADB_AUTO_UPGRADE fix its data directory needed. Deliberately no status:needs-human label: that label means the maintainer must act, and a major upgrade is agent work.
TypeScript 7 breaks Nx project-graph construction today. Hold only the 7.x line fleet-wide until Nx compatibility is proven, while leaving a later major available for its own review.

Images hosted only on LAN registries (docker-registry.lan.jlapenna.net, local/ tags) are unreachable from Renovate's hosted runner, so lookups fail as recurring 'Error obtaining docker token' repository problems. These pins are deliberate and updated by hand.

Match pnpm 11's own default 24-hour minimumReleaseAge install-time policy, for every pnpm 11 consumer. Without this, Renovate can open and auto-merge an npm bump for a package published hours ago, landing a lockfile entry that pnpm itself then rejects on the very next install (agent-lcars#1345/#1391). Consumers without npm packages are unaffected.
